findings.problem: The new `body?: object` parameter is passed straight through to `_http.post()` with no shape/allowlist check in this shared service. findings.title: post() now forwards an arbitrary caller-supplied object as JSON body with no shape validation

agent_notes: The change follows the existing pattern. RestService.post(url, body?) keeps the same pipe as sendRequest/post/delete (map handleSuccess, catchError handleError, shareReplay(1)) and only adds an optional body. Defaulting to null with `body ?? null` means the four existing no-body callers send exactly what they sent before: model-file.service.ts lines 61, 74 and 87, and server-command.service.ts line 26. No new imports, dependencies or import cycles.

Two ways to send a JSON POST now exist. bulk-command.service.ts line 118 calls HttpClient.post with a body and a typed response (BulkActionResponse | BulkErrorResponse), skipping RestService. That is a single existing site and it needs a typed JSON response, which RestService cannot give because it always uses responseType 'text' and wraps the result in WebReaction. This is under the rule of three and looks like a deliberate choice, so it is not a finding. If a third body-carrying POST shows up, decide whether RestService should support typed responses or whether typed POSTs should keep going straight to HttpClient.

Pending, outside this diff: commits 111-01 moved the backend config-set endpoint from GET to POST with a JSON body (bottle.request.json). config.service.ts set() (lines 65-68) still double-encodes the value into the URL and calls _restService.sendRequest(url), which is a GET. This diff looks like groundwork for wave 2 moving ConfigService.set onto post(url, body). Until that lands, frontend and backend disagree on the method, so settings saves will probably fail at runtime. Confirm the follow-up plan covers config.service.ts and the CONFIG_SET_URL shape. This is for the impact/bugs lanes, not an architecture finding.

tests/mocks/mock-rest.service.ts only stubs sendRequest. It has no post or delete. Once ConfigService calls post(url, body), any spec that injects MockRestService and goes through set() will need a post stub. Test scaffolding only, not a finding.

The JSDoc '@param {object} [body]' matches the signature. The 'object' type accepts arrays and class instances, which is fine for HttpClient JSON serialization. A narrower type like Record<string, unknown> would be a style choice, not an architectural concern.

agent_notes: Signature change is additive: post(url) became post(url, body?) with an optional parameter, and `body ?? null` keeps the exact old wire behavior for callers that pass no body. This is source- and runtime-compatible.

Existing post() callers I read: model-file.service.ts:61, 74 and 87 (queue/stop/extract/etc.) and server-command.service.ts:26 (restart). None of them pass a body, so they still send a null body with no JSON Content-Type. No behavior change.

When a body object is passed, Angular HttpClient serializes it as JSON and sets Content-Type: application/json automatically. That matches a backend that reads bottle.request.json, which only parses when the Content-Type is application/json.
Edge case: `body ?? null` passes falsy-but-defined values through unchanged. The `object` type already excludes primitives, so this has no practical effect.
Typing `object` is loose: it accepts arrays, Map and so on, and a Map would serialize to {}. Callers are internal, so the risk is low.

Cross-wave risk, outside this diff: in HEAD the backend config/set route is already POST+JSON, but ConfigService.set still issues a GET to the path-param URL (config.service.ts:66-68). Settings saves are therefore broken in the current tree until the frontend wave lands, so do not deploy between waves.
There are no schema or migration changes in this diff and no performance impact. The direct blast radius is limited to the 4 existing post() call sites, all unaffected.
Verdict: the diff is safe and shippable as-is. The only blocking concern is sequencing, meaning the ConfigService migration must land with it before any deploy.
